title: Mobile analytics and crash reporting (Firebase, iOS and Android)

acceptance_criteria.outcome: Mobile events use one closed catalog shared with web (catalog.v1.json, platforms web/ios/android); web and mobile contract tests fail on drift.
Analytics runs behind a provider-independent core interface with Firebase, no-op and recording providers; Firebase calls stay out of screens and business logic.
Only allowlisted events and properties are sent; unknown names, keys or values reject the whole event, and no personal, financial, receipt, token, resource-id or free-text data reaches analytics.
Analytics and crash reporting are separate opt-ins: nothing is collected before grant, revocation stops collection including in-flight work, and no pre-grant activity is replayed.
No user identifier is sent; identity and operation state reset on sign-out, forced 401 sign-out and account change, and stale-account callbacks emit nothing.
Analytics or Crashlytics failure, absence or blocking never changes product behavior or interrupts an operation.
Consent is offered once at first launch, before sign-in, with equally prominent choices, and each category is changeable in Account.
Exactly one screen_view per route-name change with stable registered names and no route parameters; Firebase automatic screen reporting is off.

Business events distinguish attempts from confirmed outcomes, emit one terminal event per operation despite retries, callbacks and re-renders, never fabricate success or replay writes, and cover the mobile-specific receipt, permission and link events.
Development, tests, E2E and web preview never reach Firebase; collection needs an explicit build environment variable; advertising identifiers and personalization are disabled on iOS and Android.

Crashlytics reports fatal and sanitized non-fatal errors with only build, version, environment and platform metadata and event-name breadcrumbs; no messages, amounts, descriptions, tokens or API responses.

Native configuration, SDK privacy manifests, privacy policy and App Store/Play Data Safety recommendations are reviewed and documented with residual risks, without claiming compliance from configuration alone.
Controlled DebugView and test-crash verification pass on a non-production Firebase project for iOS and Android, including symbolication, or the missing evidence is recorded honestly.
Existing mobile UAT, native E2E and release-readiness checklists cover both platforms, and analytics documentation extends the existing files without duplicating specifications.
